hypothesis: For any two-register machine in Wolfram's sense (program of L instructions, each 'increment register r and go to the next instruction' or 'if register r is nonzero decrement it and jump to instruction j, else go to the next instruction', cyclic program), there is an arithmetic system n -> (p*n + q)/s whose branch is chosen by n mod 6L such that, with the state (i, a, b) encoded as n = i + L * 2^a * 3^b (Wolfram's encoding on p. 673 with L = 5 and modulus 30), the integer trajectory decodes step for step to the register machine's trajectory.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered. analysis.py compiles each register machine into the remainder-selected arithmetic map, then runs machine and map side by side. Test set: (a) all 200 register machines drawn with numpy seed 20261111 from the family with L = 5 and two registers (instruction type, register and jump target uniform), each from the state (1, 0, 0) and from one random state with registers in [0, 20], for 10000 steps; (b) three hand-written programs with L in {3, 5, 7} that move or copy register contents so that the registers grow without bound, 20000 steps each. 'supports' if at every step of every run the decoded (i, a, b) equals the directly simulated register-machine state (0 mismatches out of all compared steps) and, as a check that the comparison can fail, a deliberately perturbed map (one branch's additive constant changed by 1) produces a mismatch within 10000 steps on at least one of the hand-written programs. Universality of the arithmetic systems then follows from the universality of two-register machines (Minsky 1967), which is cited, not tested.
fail_criterion: Pre-registered. 'refutes' if any run of the correctly compiled map disagrees with the register machine at any step. 'inconclusive' with reason 'other' if the perturbation check fails to produce a mismatch (the comparison would then be too weak to count).
interpretation: Wolfram's 'system that takes a whole number, computes Mod[n, 30], and applies one of several arithmetic operations chosen by that remainder' is the family of generalised Collatz maps n -> (p*n + q)/s with the branch chosen by n mod M. The specific register machine of Wolfram's figure is not transcribed in the online text, so instead of checking his single example the test checks the general construction he describes (encoding n = i + L * 2^a * 3^b, modulus 6L; for L = 5 this is his modulus 30) on a random sample of register machines plus growth programs. Register-machine conventions follow NKS Chapter 3 (pp. 97-102): decrement of a zero register is a no-op that moves to the next instruction, and the program wraps around cyclically. The 'therefore universal' clause is a theorem of Minsky's and is outside what this computation establishes.

datasets.name: Two-register machines (NKS Chapter 3 conventions) and their compiled remainder-selected arithmetic maps, generated by analysis.py: 200 random programs of length 5 (numpy seed 20261111), three hand-written growth programs of length 3, 5 and 7; 10000 or 20000 steps per run; exact Python integers
datasets.role: trajectories compared step by step between the register machine and the arithmetic system
